§C.6 Ground Truth — Inline Formatting

What to do, when producing ground truth, in the cases the inline-formatting rules leave to review. Each step serves the rule it links to; the rule decides the output.

Situation Step Rule
A drop-cap initial is genuinely unreadable Flag the page for review; do not guess the letter Drop Caps§7.2.3
A line-end hyphen cannot be classed as a break or part of the word Keep the hyphen, join the parts, and flag the word Line-End Hyphenation§7.2.7
Link anchor text differs from its target, and the target looks like it carries real meaning Keep the printed words and flag the page Links§7.2.8
An inset block is a real quotation and its quotation status looks load-bearing Flatten it as usual and flag the page Quote Blocks§7.2.9
A page carries verse or other text whose line breaks are content Apply the working default and flag the page, so it can be revisited when the open point closes Verse and Hard Line Breaks§7.2.13
